## TL;DR

Resumed task #1185 to resolve the remaining review finding: the declared capture showed Mission Control rather than the restart dialog. Added deterministic preview fixtures for the restarting and failed restart states, declared both dialog captures, and confirmed the repository QA note explicitly says no real hand-run restart was performed. The underlying implementation and detection tests were already present on this branch; this session focused on making the review evidence represent the changed restart interaction. No live server restart was performed.

## Work and rationale

The latest review report found no remaining implementation bug and specifically asked for a capture that exercises progress and error display. Existing restart fixtures showed only a pending notice, and the task did not declare shots that forced that notice to appear. I returned task #1185 to active through RepoOS before editing because the task had reached review.

I extended the shared shot fixture registry with `release:restartProgress` and `release:restartError`. The notification component now seeds a complete installed-version restart notice for these fixtures and gives both a systemd-supervised status. The progress fixture seeds the accepted restart state so the button renders “Restarting…” and stays disabled without calling a real restart endpoint. The error fixture seeds a representative supervisor failure so the modal displays its user-facing failure text and terminal recovery command. This makes the captures deterministic and safe to render in the managed preview.

I also extended the dashboard decision digest’s existing restart-fixture handling. That prevents its live loading state from competing with the restart dialog or triggering the capture loading-state guard. A unit test verifies that both fixture names produce valid shot URLs, are accepted in a declared shot plan, and are recognized as dialog captures.

Using `repoos update 1185 --shots`, I declared two shots on the app target at `/`, one per fixture, and highlighted the restart modal. This addresses the review’s evidence gap directly: reviewers can see the in-progress state and the surfaced failure state in the task’s captures.

## Approaches tried

The branch already contained the restart UI, supervisor detection, restart route, related tests, and light/dark pending fixtures. The previous review’s source inspection found no additional bug in those paths. I therefore kept the change limited to the missing preview states and declarations rather than modifying the restart behavior again. A real click-through against an external service would risk restarting an actual server and is not necessary to establish deterministic visual evidence for the two UI states.

## Challenges and blockers

The worktree was clean, but the task itself had status `review`. RepoOS guidance does not allow editing a reviewed worktree, so I changed its status back to active with the RepoOS CLI before making changes. The CLI noted that it was reading the main board while invoked from a linked worktree; the requested status transition succeeded, and all source edits were made using this worktree’s absolute path.

I did not have a real hand-run server or systemd/launchd instance under test control in this session. Accordingly, I did not claim a live restart result. The existing QA document already records “Real restart check for #1185: not performed,” and the task’s QA criterion is satisfied by that explicit statement. The automated and review capture fixtures do not replace that operator check.

## Key learnings

Review evidence needs to force the conditional UI state it is meant to verify. A generic `/` capture can be healthy and free of console errors while showing an unrelated dashboard. Registering explicit fixture states, seeding the component locally, suppressing competing page loading, and declaring the intended route and highlight makes the evidence reproducible and focused. Progress and failure states should be visually verifiable without making the screenshot runner issue a real process restart request.
